title: Ops jogwheel: tactile autoscale sculptor for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a compact, operator-focused control called the 'jogwheel' for the Redwood Console that lets on-call and platform engineers rapidly tune autoscaling parameters and burst policies for Dedicated GPU pools. The control is intended for fast incident triage and scheduled capacity tuning: a single UX that exposes burst budgets, target SLO windows, step-based autoscale curves, and a cost delta preview.

Goals: 1) Let operators make small, reversible tuning adjustments in < 30s without opening a modal. 2) Surface immediate SLO/cost tradeoffs with a lightweight simulator preview. 3) Provide safe guardrails (hard caps, preview simulation, forced review for large changes). 4) Support keyboard shortcuts and a dense UI for cockpit-style usage.

Scope: Focus on the pool-level control panel inside Dedicated > Pools > [Pool name] header. Primary controls: a central jogwheel for adjusting target concurrency (or desired GPU count), a radial selector for burst window length, quick toggles for enabling predictive autoscale, and a cost delta readout. Secondary elements: recent change history, quick rollback, current KPIs (P90 latency, unit cost, queued requests), and a lightweight simulation toggle (simulate load for X minutes).

Design decisions: - Use a radial jog metaphor to allow fine-grained + coarse adjustments via click-drag and shift/alt modifiers. - Provide 3 committed presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) and a custom mode. - Inline cost preview estimates token-per-second based cost and relative monthly delta. - When changes exceed safe thresholds (pre-configured by platform team), require canary rollout or a short approval step. - Keep visuals compact so the control can live in the top-right header and also expand into a micro-panel for more advanced edits.

Trade-offs considered: - Expressiveness vs accidental misconfiguration: mitigated by preview, undo, and confirmation thresholds. - Real-time metrics vs UI performance: initial build will use sampled metrics with a 15s refresh cadence. - Predictive autoscale UX complexity: hide advanced knobs behind 'advanced' expansion to keep primary flow simple.

Accessibility: Ensure the jogwheel is keyboard operable (arrow keys, page up/down for larger increments) and semantic labels for screen readers. Color choices follow our console palette and maintain contrast ratios for alerts.

Success metrics: - Time-to-adjust for basic scale change < 30s in usability testing. - 80% of ops tasks completed using the jogwheel within two interactions. - No increase in misconfiguration incidents after 4 weeks of early access.

Notes to engineering: Implementation will require backend API endpoints for dry-run simulation (simulate scaling for N minutes), a cost-estimation service call, and a change-commit API supporting canary rollouts.
comments: 2026-02-12 Asha: Initial whiteboard sketch completed and handed to PM. Figma file created with three states: compact, expanded micro-panel, and history modal. Link in attachments.

2026-02-18 Miguel Ortega (PM): Strong preference for cost-delta preview. Suggested adding per-tenant budget guardrails and a rollback quick action. Marking dependency on runtime cost estimator (ENG-2290).

2026-02-20 Lena Schmidt (Eng): Confirmed backend support for dry-run simulation exists but needs an API contract. Flagged potential latency for sampled metrics; suggested 15s sampling and server-side aggregation. Added ENG dependency ENG-3350 for rollout safety checks.

2026-02-24 Asha: Prototype v0.2 uploaded. Updated visuals to emphasize safety threshold and added keyboard accessibility states. Ran quick hallway usability with two SREs; both appreciated presets, one requested explicit confirmation for >20% scale increases.

2026-03-02 Design review: Feedback from Design Guild: reduce motion on jogwheel, improve label clarity for preset modes, include inline tooltip for 'burst budget'. Action: implement static numeric input fallback and microcopy updates.
2026-03-05 PM review: Miguel approved user flows and asked to add cost breakdown by token vs infrastructure for enterprise customers in expanded view. Added as follow-up scope for post-launch.
2026-03-05 Asha: Moving to 'In Review' — design handoff package ready. Next: create redlines and tokenized CSS vars for implementation, and coordinate with ENG owners for API contract doc.
next_steps: 1) Finalize API contract with ENG owners (ENG-2290, ENG-3350). 2) Produce implementation redlines and tokenized assets. 3) Run 5-user ops usability test week of 2026-03-10. 4) Hand off to engineering for sprint in 2026-W11.
